reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a cryptocurrency earning opportunity by claiming viewers can multiply Ethereum and earn up to $1,000 in commissions through Forsage. It directs viewers to create an account or sign up for bonuses, while tying participation to recruiting at least three people and purchasing increasingly expensive Ethereum-denominated slots for claimed higher profits. the available video evidence does not establish completed payments, actual returns, signup destination, or resulting losses.

citations.quote: allowing users to earn a long-term residual Ethereum income through a referral system.
Once you join, you need to refer at least three people to do the same.

Slots in each of these two programs, Fausage X3 and Fausage X4 have 12 slots. All similar and work in the same way.Each subsequent slot is two times more expensive than the previous one. Both income and profits from them are twice as high.
Sign for Wasage and get my bonuses to help you start going.

opening.argument: The presentation uses restrained, non-coercive language rather than promising a guaranteed outcome. It expressly describes the program as having “no time limit, targets, or pressure,” and explains that the smart-contract structure is intended to operate without interference from an individual operator. That framing supports an educational explanation of how the technology is supposed to function, with viewers able to assess the claims for themselves. The material also explains the mechanics of the slots and reinvestment structure rather than hiding them. Nothing in the supplied record establishes that the speaker guarantees returns, conceals the conditions, or pressures a viewer to participate.

citations.quote: The program is flexible, with no time limit, targets, or pressure.
By the fact that it runs on a smart contract, this cryptocurrency-slash-Ethereum program is immutable
All similar and work in the same way.Each subsequent slot is two times more expensive than the previous one.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s quotations show that referral participation and slot pricing were discussed, but they do not establish deception, a guaranteed return, or completed harm. Its description of “higher profits” is a statement about the program’s represented structure, not proof that the creator certified those outcomes. Likewise, a signup invitation and bonuses can accompany an explanatory presentation without proving coercion or concealment. The evidence therefore supports transparency about the claimed mechanics at least as much as it supports a finding of scam intent.

citations.quote: The program is flexible, with no time limit, targets, or pressure.
All similar and work in the same way.Each subsequent slot is two times more expensive than the previous one.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of proven losses does not resolve the content classification. The presentation links earnings to recruiting others, expressly says a participant must refer at least three people, and ends by soliciting signup and bonuses. Calling the terms flexible does not remove the recruitment-based earning mechanism, while describing a smart contract does not verify the income claims or make the arrangement non-promotional.

citations.quote: allowing users to earn a long-term residual Ethereum income through a referral system.
Once you join, you need to refer at least three people to do the same.
Sign for Wasage and get my bonuses to help you start going.

opening.argument: The central material can reasonably be read as an operational walkthrough of a software-based matrix, not as proof that viewers will profit. The narration explains what a smart contract is claimed to do, then describes the X3 and X4 slot structures, their sequencing, and how activation works. The sampled visual explicitly presents the subject as “HOW DOES FORSAGE MATRIX MARKETING WORK?”, which is consistent with demonstrating system mechanics. Explaining a referral program, even one involving cryptocurrency, does not by itself establish that the video is certifying the program as safe or guaranteeing any result. The supplied record also does not establish that any viewer joined or received money.

citations.quote: How Fausage Matrix works.
Slots in each of these two programs, Fausage X3 and Fausage X4 have 12 slots.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats instructional detail as solicitation, but a tutorial must explain the very features being demonstrated. The narration’s focus on smart-contract immutability and the slot layout is technical and descriptive; it does not document a completed transaction, prove that the speaker received commissions, or establish that the displayed claims are factual. Even the referral language can be understood as part of explaining how the system operates. Without evidence of a deceptive act or realized loss, the educational reading remains plausible.

citations.quote: the smart contract is a constituted blockchain technology that describes an automated digital contract that cannot be broken or changed
How many slots can be activated immediately? As much as you want.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational explanation is embedded in promotion, not presented as neutral analysis. The same material says users can earn residual Ethereum through referrals, instructs each entrant to refer three people, and asks viewers to sign up for bonuses. The visual heading may describe the topic, but it does not show that the creator is warning viewers or testing the system. Technical explanation therefore does not negate the recruitment solicitation.

citations.quote: allowing users to earn a long-term residual Ethereum income through a referral system.
Once you join, you need to refer at least three people to do the same.

opening.argument: The evidence is also compatible with promotion of an online service or referral opportunity whose mechanics are openly described. The record does not show a request for credentials, a completed deposit, a verified payout, or an actual loss. It describes a smart-contract-based service, identifies the slot progression, and says users may activate slots; those facts alone do not establish that the service is fraudulent. Even the displayed account-style material cannot be treated as independent proof either way. A careful classification should not infer a scam solely from cryptocurrency terminology, referral language, or an invitation to create an account when the supplied evidence does not establish the missing deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: Falsage.io is a crypto earning program that operates on a smart contract.
How many slots can be activated immediately? As much as you want.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a referral structure, but referral promotion is not automatically fraudulent commerce. Its quoted slot language describes prices and claimed returns without showing that money was taken from a viewer or that the claim was knowingly false. The displayed account and commission material may be promotional, yet they still do not establish a credential request, completed payment, or loss. On the supplied record, the required deceptive mechanism remains unproven.

citations.quote: Once you join, you need to refer at least three people to do the same.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is more than an ordinary product referral: the stated income is residual Ethereum income generated through recruiting, and participation requires bringing in at least three additional people. The sampled promotion also combines an account-creation prompt with a commission claim. Completed loss is unnecessary to identify the mechanism being promoted; the video itself supplies the recruitment and tiered-slot structure.
